issues: Non-blocking: in reading_story the keyword 'UNIVERSAL' sits mid-sentence ('swells into a UNIVERSAL anthem, ringing...') rather than strictly at start/end; the start/end gate is satisfied by the main story, so this is fine, but the reading-story payoff could be tightened to the clause end.

Non-blocking: 'solar panels' is invented scene glue (not a kanji component); it validly fuses 並 'row' + 日 'Sun' and is not treated as an actor, so it is not a phantom, but it is the one piece of non-component imagery to keep an eye on.

story: VIOLENCE: the midday Sun blazes overhead as a mob, hands raised TOGETHER, stampedes forward — and beneath their feet a towering Tsunami Wave rears up, curling to smash everything to splinters.
reading_story: Bowie, drenched, screams into the mic as the Tsunami Wave floods the stage — pure onstage VIOLENCE, spray flying over the front row.

story: A sturdy bare Tree crashes down; loggers saw its straight trunk, lop off the two upward branches, and haul away neat golden planks of LUMBER.
reading_story: Zy, the heavy-jawed twin, strains under a shoulder-load of stacked LUMBER, the boards creaking as he stomps them into his truck.
issues: Distinctiveness is moderate: the generic 'tree felled and cut into planks = lumber' logging imagery risks interference with neighboring wood/board-radical kanji such as 板 (board/plank) or 林/森 (forest); the specific hooks (crashing tree, golden planks, Zy) keep it above threshold but it is not strongly individuated.

story: A lone TREE stands at the edge of the clearing while a Tape Measure, tongue quivering, stretches one inch out beside its trunk to survey the tidy huts of the VILLAGE.
reading_story: Sonny leans against the crooked signpost, grinning as he welcomes every traveler into the little mountain VILLAGE.

story: A single sturdy bare Tree, two branches flung skyward and two roots clutching earth, stands—then hundreds more identical Trees crowd in around it, trunks packed tight into one cool, whispering GROVE.
reading_story: Lynn wanders off the trail and vanishes into the shadowy GROVE, calling out as endless tree trunks swallow her voice.
issues: Distinctiveness risk: generic tree-multiplication overlaps heavily with the close neighbor 森 (forest), especially since the record's own meanings list both Grove and Forest; the grove-vs-forest boundary is not sharply cued.
Reading story does not reinforce the reading actor's noted feature ('Lynn ... ends in -n'); the -n ending is not encoded in Lynn's action.
Keyword GROVE lands well at the end of the meaning story but sits mid-sentence in the reading story (non-blocking, as the placement gate applies to the meaning story).

story: The detective props a bare Tree against a wooden Stacked Shelf Crate, lifting each slatted shelf to peer between the boxes as he INVESTIGATES what's hidden inside.
reading_story: Sah pries open the shelf crate at the crime scene, magnifier raised, muttering as she INVESTIGATES every dusty box.

story: A sturdy bare Tree stands alone in a field, and you tug on the thick tendril spreading below its trunk — dragging up its deepest, gnarled ROOT, dirt clinging everywhere.
reading_story: Sean Connery — Conn — kneels and grips a stubborn ROOT, yanking it from the soil while muttering in his gravel brogue.
issues: Non-blocking: 'tendril' is botanically imprecise for a root (tendrils are climbing organs, not roots); 'spreading below its trunk' salvages the image but slightly muddies the vivid picture.

Distinctiveness is moderate (3): 'bare tree + root being pulled up' risks interference with wood-family neighbors, especially 本 (origin/base-of-tree, literally 木 marked at its root); the tugging action and Conn's on'yomi reading_story mitigate this.

Minor consistency nuance: reading こん is short-vowel (per doc 07 §1.2 short vowels get a 'clipped/shrunken twin'), but the reading_story presents Conn as a full persona with no brevity signaling. Not a gate failure.

story: One sturdy Tree stands tall on the ridge; below it, two more Trees root themselves side by side—three bare trunks crowding together into a dense, whispering FOREST.
reading_story: Behind his bar, Shinn pours a final nightcap, locks the door, and walks home through the pitch-dark FOREST where three black trees loom.
issues: Record inconsistency (non-gating, upstream): dominant_reading is kun もり but reading_actor is on'yomi しん (Shinn). Per doc §1.3, kun'yomi get no reading actor (should be null with no reading story). The reading_story teaches しん, not the dominant もり — it anchors the wrong reading and should be fixed in the record.
Minor: in reading_story the keyword FOREST is not the final word ('...FOREST where three black trees loom'); acceptable for a reading story but worth noting.
Distinctiveness is only moderate — 'forest = trees' is near-tautological; interference risk with 林 (woods/two trees) is mitigated but not eliminated by foregrounding the three-tree count.

story: The Tree hoists its straight trunk upright, drives its spreading roots deep into the wet soil, and settles firm — a freshly PLANTED sapling shivering with new leaves.
reading_story: Shocker the wrestler grips a sapling like a folding chair and slams it root-first into the ring, PLANTING it dead center to a roaring crowd.

story: At Earth's frozen POLES, a lone Tree shivers beside an Open Mouth gasping clouds, while a yellow Rubber Glove rests palm-up on the flat white Horizon Line stretching endlessly.
reading_story: Kyoker plants a flag at both POLES, panting in the cutting cold, claiming each icy extreme of the frozen planet as his own.

story: A sturdy Tree leans across a river. A Falling Katana slashes its top plank, an Open Mouth gapes below, and a Goalpost Frame arches over water — together forming a walkable BRIDGE.
reading_story: Kyo the frontman howls from the middle of the BRIDGE, guitar screaming as fans crowd both banks below him.
issues: Spatial assembly is slightly busy: 'slashes its top plank', 'gapes below', 'arches over water' layer three separate positions rather than fusing into one clean picture, so imageability is good but not effortless.
Resolution 'together forming a walkable BRIDGE' is a soft/generic bridge-assembly, capping distinctiveness.

story: A Yawning Cavern gapes in a white cliff, cold air sighing from its empty hollow — and carved above its lip, the whole continent of EUROPE spreads across the rockface.
reading_story: Owen presses his ear to the Yawning Cavern and hears every language of EUROPE echoing up from the dark.

story: At the slanting Ritual Stake, all motion grinds to a STOP — none may pass. The lone figure who plants himself there, holding the ground unbudged, is the WARRIOR.
reading_story: Tiny Boo toddles up in her monster costume, roars, and stamps both feet, declaring herself the fiercest WARRIOR in the whole closet.
issues: Advisory (non-blocking): the 止 'stop' beat is rendered as 'all motion grinds to a STOP — none may pass', which is abstract because 止 supplies only a keyword with no concrete actor; imageability would improve with a concrete thing being halted at the stake.

story: Beneath the jutting Rock Overhang, an ancient grove of trees has stopped growing — every trunk frozen mid-reach, silently recording the slow PASSAGE OF TIME.
reading_story: Recker leans against the frozen grove and carves a notch for every year, tallying the endless PASSAGE OF TIME.

story: Two identical twins stand shoulder to shoulder on a bathroom scale, craning to COMPARE which one is a hair taller.
reading_story: Hee snatches both report cards, holds them side by side, and giggles "hee!" as she COMPARES the two grades.

story: Puddle Splash hurls three fat droplets that swell and swell into a churning current, wider than any stream — a great RIVER (LARGE) carving the valley.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr misjudges the ford and his taxi floats off down the swollen RIVER (LARGE), horn blaring as the current sweeps him away.

story: Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets off to the left, mid-air. They land slick and rainbow-sheened, refusing to soak in — this whole puddle is pure OIL.
reading_story: Hugh crouches, dips a rag into the slick puddle, and wrings thick OIL from it, black droplets staining his fingers.
issues: Advisory (non-blocking): dominant_reading is kun あぶら but a ゆ on-reading actor (Hugh) is attached, which sits in tension with rubric §1.3 (kun'yomi get no reading actor). This is a record-level data choice, not a candidate defect.

story: Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets off to the left, mid-splash, scattering down toward the puddle spreading across the tiles — vivid proof of the flooded room's soggy CONDITION.
reading_story: Onstage, Kyo the howling frontman hurls his mic skyward mid-scream, sweat spraying off him, growling about the crumbling venue's dismal CONDITION.

story: The Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets off to the left, and they sparkle so clean the roadside puddle below turns crystal-clear and utterly PURE.
reading_story: High on the peak, a white-bearded Sage cups the icy spring, sips slowly, and pronounces the water utterly PURE.
issues: Non-blocking: the meaning story is near-tautological (clean pure water = 'pure'), which caps distinctiveness against neighboring water/clean kanji; the concrete Puddle-Splash and peak-Sage hooks keep it just distinct enough.

story: Puddle Splash flicks droplets left as a Barbed Pike stabs a wide-open Open Mouth, a Meat Hook snagging its tongue — the puddle shrinks, the shout thins, everything DWINDLES to nothing.

story: Three droplets from a Puddle Splash scatter left into a curved Longbow bent like a coastline; a Pot Lid clamps over the bow's top, sealing the crescent of water into a calm BAY.
reading_story: Wann paddles his kayak into the sheltered BAY, laughing as the calm water curves around him.

story: SEMI-frozen: Puddle Splash's three fat droplets hang left of the puddle, each half-crusted in ice, the lower halves still liquid and quivering, caught exactly between splash and freeze.
reading_story: SEMI-melted, the fountain sags as June scoops one droplet of Puddle Splash, half water and half slush, dribbling through her chilled fingers.

story: A BOMB rolls into the crackling BONFIRE, its sparks licking the fuse until the whole thing detonates in a roaring fireball.

Advisory (non-blocking): the scene is near-tautological (keyword 'bomb' encoded as a bomb exploding); generic explosion/fire imagery keeps distinctiveness at a modest 3 with some interference risk against neighbouring fire/burst kanji.

story: The Kings Crown sits on its velvet cushion; one glossy black Ink Droplet slips off the brush, lands in the crown's hollow, and freezes there into a single glittering JEWEL.
reading_story: Heavy-set Gyocker plucks the JEWEL from the crown, gripping it in his thick fist so tightly the gem's cut facets bite deep into his palm.
issues: Minor (non-gating): the Ink Droplet 'freezes into a jewel' is a transformation rather than the droplet's defined 'make one tiny dot' action; acceptable as the imaginative keyword payoff and spatially it lands where the 丶 dot sits, but it slightly stretches the persona's stated behavior.

Minor (non-gating): crown/jewel/gem imagery is a somewhat generic cluster with modest interference risk against other jewelry/treasure-themed kanji, though the droplet-as-dot device does well to separate 玉 from its lookalike 王 (king).

story: By the Leaning Sickbed, a Sand Trickle sprinkles down onto the blazing Sun, which warms Twin Pillars propping an open Stepladder — and the fevered patient is HEALED.
reading_story: Ryo the hardboiled detective pours whiskey over his knife wound in a back alley, grits his teeth, and by morning the ragged gash has HEALED clean.
issues: Meaning story's middle causal chain (sand sprinkling onto the sun, sun warming pillars that prop a ladder) is a loose, arbitrary Rube-Goldberg sequence rather than one cohesive scene, limiting memorability.
'Fevered patient' is borderline extra narrative but is acceptable as the payoff-object of the 'heal' keyword (the 疒 sickbed image is defined as 'waiting for a patient'), not a phantom component.
With five components packed in, the meaning scene is slightly cluttered; the reading story is notably stronger and more distinctive than the meaning story.

story: Behind the marble desk of the GOVERNMENT MINISTRY, a single enormous Watching Eye sits enthroned, its dark pupil swiveling to inspect every clerk, every stamped form, every whispered bribe in the vast hall.
reading_story: The top-hatted Showman flings open the GOVERNMENT MINISTRY doors and bellows "Shoooow!", parading trembling bureaucrats across a red-carpet stage like circus acts.
issues: meaning_placement field declares 'end' but the keyword GOVERNMENT MINISTRY actually lands at the START of the story ('Behind the marble desk of the GOVERNMENT MINISTRY...') — metadata inconsistency; gate 4 still passes since start is a valid position.

Distinctiveness is only moderate: an all-seeing 'Watching Eye' surveilling a government bureaucracy is a well-worn trope (Big Brother / panopticon), and government+eye is a somewhat predictable pairing; the specific ministry scene rescues it but it risks blending with other 目-based stories.

story: A giant Watching Eye hovers above the map, its dark pupil fixed downward as a thin Sand Trickle scatters three grains onto the border of one PREFECTURE.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll plants a flag at the PREFECTURE line, grinning stiffly as the whole province salutes his molded arm.

story: On the measuring table a Feathered Arrow lies to the left of a Stemmed Goblet on the right; propped beside the goblet's proud stem, the arrow suddenly looks absurdly SHORT.
reading_story: The Tanner snips his leather strap too eagerly, then holds up one SHORT, stubby belt and curses his overzealous shears.

story: A dark GROVE of twin trees looms overhead, and beneath them a giant hand SHOWS a red-lettered sign to every hiker — the trees themselves spelling out one word: PROHIBITION.
reading_story: King stands below the tall GROVE and SHOWS the marching crowd a placard, his fist raised, thundering the one command they must obey: PROHIBITION.
issues: Distinctiveness limited: 'sign prohibiting entry to a grove/forest' is a somewhat generic trope that could interfere with neighboring forest/prohibition kanji (non-blocking).
Meaning story payoff 'the trees themselves spelling out one word' is a mildly abstract image compared to the otherwise concrete scene (non-blocking).
'giant hand' enacts the 示/show action as ordinary agency; acceptable but borderline as an added prop.

story: A golden Rice Stalk bends low over the paddy, its heavy head nudging a thin orange Crescent Moon sideways across the dusk water in one smooth SHIFT.
reading_story: Eaton nails the Crescent Moon sign above his barn door, then steps back to watch its orange light SHIFT along the wall.

story: On the right, my elder brother hoists Twin Pillars overhead; to his left a golden Rice Stalk leans in. He surrenders its heavy grain as TAX.
reading_story: Zay, a heavy-voiced official, booms down the market demanding TAX, sealing each merchant's ledger with his loud, thumping stamp.
issues: Reading story places 'TAX' mid-sentence ('demanding TAX') rather than at start/end; non-blocking since keyword placement is gated on the meaning story (where it lands at the end) and the reading story's payoff is correctly the reading actor Zay.
Meaning scene is slightly busy (elder brother hoisting pillars overhead AND surrendering grain are two loci), keeping imageability at 4 rather than 5.

story: Two sprinters STAND UP at the blocks, each copying the other's every twitch and lean, muscles quivering as they strain to EMULATE and outdo their mirror-image rival.
reading_story: Kyo, the howling rock frontman, screams into the mic; a hundred garage bands rise to EMULATE his throat-ripping long ō, each vowing to out-howl the legend.

story: Side by side in the Bamboo Grove, two tall green stalks creak in the wind, their drooping leaf-tufts hanging over like paired brushstrokes — pure BAMBOO.
reading_story: A Chicker hops between the twin stalks, drumming its beak on each hollow BAMBOO cane until the whole grove rings.
issues: Non-blocking: BAMBOO in reading_story falls mid-sentence ('each hollow BAMBOO cane'); placement gate is satisfied by the main story's end placement, so this is not a failure.
Non-blocking: core bamboo-grove-in-wind imagery is somewhat generic; distinctiveness rests mainly on the brushstroke leaf-tufts and the ringing drummed cane.

story: A Bamboo Grove sways overhead as a giant Watching Eye scans the ledger below, while two Cupped Palms lift up beads to tally each row — that is how you CALCULATE.
reading_story: Santa perches under the bamboo, a lone Watching Eye peering as his Cupped Palms flick abacus beads to CALCULATE which children were nice.
issues: Reading story abbreviates 竹's actor to 'the bamboo' rather than the full registry persona 'Bamboo Grove' (main story uses the full name correctly) — a minor actor-consistency slip, not gating.

Distinctiveness risk: the abacus/bead 'calculate' motif is meaning-generic and could interfere with neighboring number/counting kanji; the unique component anchors (eye + cupped palms + bamboo) keep it at an acceptable level.
Reading-story keyword 'CALCULATE which children were nice' places the payoff verb near but not at the very end; acceptable since the main story carries clean end placement and it is not buried.

story: A Bamboo Grove's two tall stalks, naturally hollow, lean together and channel rainwater straight down through their joined green stems, forming one long, dripping PIPE.
reading_story: Khan raises a hollowed bamboo stalk like a war-horn PIPE and blows a booming signal that rallies his galloping horde across the steppe.
issues: Non-blocking: in the reading story, PIPE sits mid-sentence ('like a war-horn PIPE and blows...') rather than as a terminal payoff; acceptable since the reading story's primary job is encoding かん/Khan, but the keyword is slightly buried there.

Non-blocking: bamboo-forming-a-pipe is a semantically on-the-nose image with interference risk against neighboring 竹-radical tube/wind kanji (e.g. 筒 tube, 笛 flute); the rainwater-drip specificity and the Khan war-horn hook are what keep it distinct (distinctiveness=3).

story: Cast flat above the entrance, a wide FISHING NET drapes its mesh grid down over the front desk, snagging every fleeing suspect the moment they bolt from the POLICE STATION.
reading_story: Shaw strolls into the POLICE STATION, flashing a grin as the desk sergeant recognizes the famous playwright and waves him straight past the front counter.
issues: Reading story places 'POLICE STATION' mid-sentence (4th word) rather than strictly at start/end; non-blocking since the meaning story governs placement and correctly ends on the keyword.

Distinctiveness risk: the net-snags-fleeing-criminals motif could interfere with sibling 罒 kanji (e.g. 罪 crime, 罰 punishment); the police-station 'front desk / desk sergeant' framing mitigates but does not eliminate this.

story: On the black windowpane, two Frost Beads of ice cling and glint. Just below them on the sill lie the Feather Pair — two matching white FEATHERS, barbed vanes curving up from a vanished bird.
reading_story: Ooh the crooner holds one long, quivering "ooh," and with the breath two loose FEATHERS drift up off his velvet lapel and float away.

story: Against the low Full Moon, three fresh Bean Sprouts poke up, and just below them yawns a Spiked Pit with crossed stakes — this eerie tableau is exactly the anatomy of a BRAIN.
reading_story: Noah, cradling the last dove, taps his skull and swears the whole ark's map lives inside his BRAIN.

story: A Grass Tuft crowns the stage; beneath it a Sealed Clam-Locket cracks open on two gleaming Railway Tracks, spilling a hidden treasure — pure ACTING, a private secret finally performed.
reading_story: Gei kneels on the Railway Tracks, prying the Clam-Locket open, and out bursts her greatest ACTING role — a hidden performance long sealed away.
issues: All three mandatory components named with correct personas: ⺾ Grass Tuft, 二 Railway Tracks, 厶 Sealed Clam-Locket.
No phantom component actors: 'stage' and 'treasure' are narrative dressing (performance context / locket's hidden contents), not introduced as kanji components.
Clam-Locket cracking open to reveal a hidden private thing is ordinary physical motion consistent with its defined nature (sealed shut, private secret curled inside) — no invented cognitive ability.
Reading actor 'Gei' present in reading_story; reading actor non-null and correctly used.
meaning_placement=end honored: keyword ACTING sits in the final clause of the main story.
No etymology referenced; both stories under ~40 words (story ~29, reading_story ~23).

Minor (non-blocking): ACTING is followed by 'a private secret finally performed' rather than being the literal last word, and the component→'acting' link leans slightly abstract, softening imageability.

story: The lone Tailor's Lapel, pinned to the dummy's left edge with its thread dangling, is stitched onto a bare shirt as an extra folded flap — a SUPPLEMENT of fabric widening the too-narrow coat.
reading_story: Hoth, shivering on the ice planet, tears a spare pelt into a SUPPLEMENT and sews it over his thinning parka.
issues: Keyword placement is borderline: 'a SUPPLEMENT of fabric widening the too-narrow coat' puts SUPPLEMENT as the head of the final clause but with a five-word trailing modifier, so it is near-end rather than strictly terminal. meaning_placement claims 'end'; passes as the semantic climax of the last clause but is not a clean end-position.

The tailoring/patching scene (adding extra fabric to clothing) is a natural but somewhat generic frame for a 衤 (cloth-radical) kanji, creating mild interference risk with other clothing-radical characters — this caps distinctiveness.

story: The Speech Bubble hovers on the left, dictating orders; to its right, the Lance-Butt Grip jabs the blunt lance-end into fresh earth, staking out a brand-new ESTABLISHMENT.
reading_story: Settler Seth plants the final fencepost, dusts off his hands, and declares his frontier ESTABLISHMENT officially open for business.

story: A Speech Bubble on the left, lid flipped open, recites to the class: atop a sturdy Tree balances a flooded Rice-Paddy Grid — today's LESSON in growing rice from seedling to harvest.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr pulls over, clipped and curt, and drills the nervous learner-driver on one hard LESSON: never miss the same turn twice.

story: The Speech Bubble floats over the market, its lid flipping open to fling out stacked lines of words — labels raining onto VARIOUS stalls of fruit, cloth, and spice below.
reading_story: Shaw leans on his cane, tipping his hat at the VARIOUS actors, critics, and stagehands crowding the theatre lobby around him.
issues: Keyword 'various' is conveyed generically in both stories by attaching it as an adjective to a plural noun ('VARIOUS stalls', 'VARIOUS actors, critics, and stagehands'), which is a weaker distinctiveness hook than dramatizing variety itself.

In the meaning story VARIOUS sits in the final clause but is followed by a 7-word tail ('stalls of fruit, cloth, and spice below'), so it reads as late-middle rather than strictly terminal; acceptable as 'end' placement but not the last word.

story: At the podium's left, the Speech Bubble flips its lid open and lets its stacked lines of words pour out, sentence after dull sentence — a droning, endless LECTURE.
reading_story: Sebastian Coe sprints to the lectern, still panting from his race, and delivers a breathless LECTURE on running to the packed auditorium.

story: The Twin Ski Slopes lean in from a high peak, two snowy walls angling steeply down until they pinch shut at a dark notch — the narrow VALLEY cradled between them.
reading_story: Coker straps in and carves the Twin Ski Slopes, plunging through their shadowed notch into the deep VALLEY where the two ridges finally meet.

story: BOUNTIFUL is the harvest: atop the Stemmed Goblet, a heaped mound of grain BENDS the shelf beneath it, spilling wheat down over the little splayed legs of the wide flat base.
reading_story: Ho, jolly in red, tips his Stemmed Goblet so BOUNTIFUL cider floods the table, and belts "ho-ho-ho!"
issues: Component 曲 'bend' is integrated only as a throwaway verb ('BENDS the shelf') on invented scenery rather than a vivid object anchor — coverage passes but the element is weakly imageable.
Distinctiveness capped at 3: the 'bountiful harvest/grain' theme is semantically on-the-nose and risks interference with neighboring abundance kanji (e.g. 富 rich/abundant).

story: A Swaddling Wrap curls down from above and hugs a Muddy Boar so tightly its snout stretches into a trunk — behold, a bristly little ELEPHANT.
reading_story: The top-hatted Showman flings his cape over the ELEPHANT and bellows "Shoooow!" as the great grey beast rears on its stubby legs.

story: Under a draped BEDSHEET COVER, a lone CARTWHEEL rolls itself across the battlefield — a hidden war chariot leading the vast marching ARMY.
reading_story: General Gunn raises his sabre; his ARMY thunders forward, boots and wheels drumming the cracked earth into rising dust.
issues: Non-blocking: 'a hidden war chariot' is an emergent fusion of the cover+cartwheel, not a phantom actor, but it edges close to the true etymology of 軍 (chariot under encirclement) — acceptable here since it is framed as an imaginative scene, not an etymological claim.
Non-blocking: slight scale jump from 'a lone CARTWHEEL' to 'leading the vast marching ARMY' in one sentence.

story: A wooden cartwheel rolls left, TRANSPORTING its cargo: a stepladder perched on top, and beneath it a full moon glowing beside a guillotine blade poised at the right edge, ready to drop.
reading_story: Hugh loads crates onto his cart and TRANSPORTS them across town before dawn, the wheels never once stopping.

story: A BEND in the stepped green hillside cradles the Razor-Clam Hoe below, its pale foot thrusting out to slice the soil into neat furrows — the birthplace of all AGRICULTURE.
reading_story: Noah abandons his ark for AGRICULTURE, planting vineyards across the drained mud in tidy rows the moment the floodwaters recede.

story: A rubber CONVEYOR BELT crawls along the road's edge, and dangling just above it a broad butcher's CLEAVER swings, its blade grazing every crate that trundles past through the VICINITY.
reading_story: Henson leans over the workshop rail, guiding his felt puppet just past the whirring blade, keeping it safe within the cluttered VICINITY of the stage.

story: A rubber CONVEYOR BELT hums along the road's bottom edge, ferrying a glowing scroll of REVELATION forward — and from that carried prophecy, a whole new world blinks into being. CREATE.
reading_story: Zoe unrolls the scroll of REVELATION and, word by spoken word, watches a mountain, a river, a city CREATE themselves before her eyes.
issues: Non-blocking: 'a whole new world blinks into being' is a generic creation trope, creating mild interference risk with other create/make/build kanji (distinctiveness ceiling).
Non-blocking: reading_story anchors the reading actor (Zoe) and 告 (revelation) but omits the 辶 conveyor belt; acceptable since reading stories only require the reading actor.

story: Horizon Sunrise balances atop the Village Milestone, its first light spilling across the flooded paddy fields below to reveal every heaped basket at market — the harvest's full QUANTITY.
reading_story: Ryo, the hardboiled detective, thumbs the warehouse ledger, growling as he counts the exact QUANTITY of stolen crates stacked to the rafters.

story: The gleaming, pyramid-topped Gold Ingot, two flecks glinting at its base, tarnishes overnight into a cold, magnetic bar of dull grey IRON.
reading_story: Tetsuo slams his fist against the subway train's hull, and the whole car rings — solid IRON — as it screams through the tunnel.

story: A gleaming Gold Ingot slams onto the courtroom table, its two glinting flecks catching the light — evidence so heavy the clerk stamps it forever into the official RECORD.
reading_story: A Rocker slams his final chord; the studio needle etches the roar onto spinning vinyl — his loudest, most defiant RECORD.

story: Two towering wooden doors, hinged and symmetrical, groan apart on iron pins to reveal the walled city beyond — the mighty GATE swinging wide.

story: A monsoon flood surges at the village, but the Terraced Hill's stacked earthen ledges catch and split each wave, its zigzag footpath sluicing the water aside — the terraces WARD OFF the deluge.

issues: Minor (non-blocking): the main story's 'terraced hill wards off a flood' pairing is somewhat on-the-nose, restating the defend/protect/resist meanings via a common water-defense trope; the concrete details (zigzag footpath sluicing, split waves) keep it distinctive enough.

story: On the Terraced Hill's zigzag ledges, a Mound of Soil sits heaped atop the two stubby stone Wishing-Well Legs, and together this stacked, earthy tower stands as dry, solid LAND.

issues: Main story is right at the ~40-word ceiling (approx 39-40 words), leaving no margin.

story: A raw hide stretches across the wooden Tanning Rack, pinned taut at every corner, baking stiff and flat under the blazing sun until it cures into gleaming LEATHER.

story: A GUEST steps in from the left; to his right stands a big pale Cracked Conch, propped upright. He tips forward, pressing its cool spiral crown against his sweating FOREHEAD.

story: A dentist counts a tooth to STOP guessing your YEARS: over the Trap Pit, Scattered Rice Grains rain down, a Stepladder straddles the rim, and a Wax Stamp bows to certify each decade.
reading_story: Ray runs a wrinkled thumb along a worn tooth, drawls the birth-date, and announces the exact number of YEARS behind that fading smile.
issues: Meaning story is two loosely-joined scenes (dentist counting a tooth, then a static prop tableau over the pit) linked only by a colon; the second half reads as a placed-object list rather than an interacting event, weakening cohesion.
The '米 = Scattered Rice Grains' image specifies grains flung 'in all directions'; 'rain down' narrows this to a single downward direction (minor persona drift, still consistent with scattering).
An unnamed 'dentist' is introduced as the framing agent; acceptable as narrative glue but adds a non-component character to the scene.
